printed: Genital herpes can also be due to HSV1 infection, and a study in Scotland found that 40% of genital herpes was due to HSV1 in 1991 [Ross et al., 1993]. Both HSV1 and HSV2 are able to infect and reactivate in the same anatomic area, although the natural history of these infections is markedly different, with HSV2 recurring more frequently than HSV1, so most clinical reactivations are likely to be due to HSV2 [Sucato et al., 1998]. In developing countries, the proportion of genital herpes caused by HSV1 is unknown, although assumed to be low.
